Understanding complex trafc patterns has become more challenging in the context of rapidly growing city road networks,
especially with the rise of Internet of Vehicles (IoV) systems that add further dynamics to trafc fow management. Tis involves
understanding spatial relationships and nonlinear temporal associations. Accurately predicting trafc in these scenarios, par-
ticularly for long-term sequences, is challenging due to the complexity of the data involved in smart city contexts. Traditional ways
of predicting trafc fow use a single fxed graph structure based on the location. Tis structure does not consider possible
correlations and cannot fully capture long-term temporal relationships among trafc fow data, making predictions less accurate.
We propose a novel trafc prediction framework called Multi-scale Attention-Based Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolution
Recurrent Network (MASTGCNet) to address this challenge. MASTGCNet records changing features of space and time by
combining gated recurrent units (GRUs) and graph convolution networks (GCNs). Its design incorporates multiscale feature
extraction and dual attention mechanisms, efectively capturing informative patterns at diferent levels of detail. Furthermore,
MASTGCNet employs a resource allocation strategy within edge computing to reduce energy usage during prediction. Te
attention mechanism helps quickly decide which services are most important. Using this information, smart cities can assign tasks
and allocate resources based on priority to ensure high-quality service. We have tested this method on two diferent real-world
datasets and found that MASTGCNet predicts signifcantly better than other methods. Tis shows that MASTGCNet is a step
forward in trafc prediction.

3.1. Model Framework. Te attention layer, encoder layer,
and prediction layer are the three primary layers that
comprise the MASTGCNet model framework. Te trafc
data are initially converted using a tanh activation function

bedding block is then used to capture complicated patterns.
After that, the trafc data are analyzed through several
spatiotemporal attention (ST-Attention) layers to identify
geographical and temporal correlations. Te encoded data
are sent to the encoder layer, which manages temporal
patterns and dynamic trafc variations using multiscale

Generation Networks (DGGNs). After the trafc fows are
adjusted, they enter the prediction layer, where a GCN is
used to capture spatial dependencies, and a sequence of
ResUnits further develop deep representations. Ultimately,
the prediction output is generated by a fully connected (FC)
layer, which uses the processed data to represent the ex-
pected trafc fows.

Te time and space complexities of Algorithm 1 are
closely related to key parameters, mainly the amount of
available historical information and the number of features.
In particular, the complexities depend on two crucial factors:
the training time, denoted by m, which is the time required
to form the dataset D, and the learning time, denoted by n,
which characterizes the time required to acquire knowledge
within the model while keeping the computational overhead
for θ constant. It is important to understand that the al-
gorithm’s performance shows diferent behaviors under
diferent circumstances. In the best-case scenario, the al-
gorithm exhibits a time complexity denoted by ω(m + n). In
this case, the computational cost escalates linearly with both
training and learning times. Tis scenario represents an
optimal match of algorithm efciency with available com-
putational resources, culminating in a favorable perfor-
mance profle. Conversely, the worst-case scenario reveals
a potentially signifcant time complexity that can rise to
O((mn)(m + n)) and further simplifes to O(m2n + n2m).
Tis particular scenario depends on the number of obser-
vations and the dimensionality of the features. Tis worst-
case behavior serves as a stark reminder of the paramount
importance of carefully considering resource constraints and
dataset characteristics when implementing Algorithm 1.
6. Related Works
In this section, we emphasize how we use deep learning to
understand the spatiotemporal correlation for trafc pre-
diction. We also look closer at the concept of attention,
which plays an important role in our model.
6.1. Trafc Flow Prediction. In the feld of trafc prediction,
the incorporation of predictive spatial information is
emerging as a key factor. Modern methods using convo-
lution neural networks (CNNs) [27, 28] for trafc fow
mapping often rely on grid-based map segmentation.
However, the inherent regularity of grid-based data limits
their ability to represent complex spatial information ef-
fectively. Reference [29] proposed a unique multitask spa-
tiotemporal network for highway trafc fow prediction
(MT-STNet) that combines multitask learning, generative
inference system, and encoder–decoder structure. Refer-
ences [30, 31] (DCRNN) innovatively presented a difusion
convolution RNN based on distance graphs. Teir approach
incorporates bidirectional random walks on the graph to
capture spatial dependencies.
However, the establishment of spatial topology in
these methods through predefned adjacency matrices
remains static and limited in nature, with inherent lim-
itations in encapsulating the complex characteristics of
complex road networks. Existing methods based on
predefned graph structures face signifcant challenges.
First, predefned graph constructs struggle with sparsity
issues. Sparsity, which is particularly evident in large
graphs, manifests itself in the adjacency matrix, leading to
computationally inefcient operations and may fail to
encapsulate the totality of spatial dependencies compre-
hensively. Tis, in turn, can potentially undermine the
accuracy of the model [32]. A secondary concern revolves
around the infexible nature of predefned adjacency
matrices, which makes them ill-suited for accommodating
dynamic graphs or graphs characterized by recurrent
structural changes [33].
In conjunction with the previous discourse on the
construction of spatial topology, the strategic modeling of
spatial and temporal dependencies emerges as a key factor in
trafc prediction. Capturing temporal dependencies re-
quires recourse to rRNNs and their diversifcation, which are
expertly tailored to sequential data with intrinsic capabilities
to capture temporal correlations of a temporal nature
[34, 35]. Te recurrent nature of RNN operations provides
increased model fexibility. In Ref. [36], this paper proposes
a unique deep learning approach to improve trafc volume
forecasting accuracy by addressing these shortcomings. In
order to create synthetic data or synthetic trafc volume,
a new spatiotemporal dependencies generative adversarial
network are frst proposed.
In contrast to the more complicated LSTM [37], GRU
advocates a simpler and more trainable architecture. Gaining
prominence for their efectiveness and versatility, attention
mechanisms [38] have found widespread application in
various domains. Tese mechanisms automatically focus on
central information extracted from historical input data.
Graph attention networks (GANs) [5] have made signifcant
progress in trafc prediction by constructing spatial models.
STSGCN [39] introduces a novel concept by devising a syn-
chronized GCN model for spatial and temporal aspects. Tese
modules adeptly capture correlations across space and time.

6.2. Attention Mechanism. Te attention mechanism has
become an important tool in various tasks such as language
translation and image recognition, helping to decide which
parts are most important to focus on Ref. [41]. Tis
mechanism uses a process where a question and a set of key-
value pairs create an output. Te output is a mixture of the
values, with the importance of each value determined using
a compatibility function between the question and its key.
Attention mechanisms are generally used in conjunction
with convolutional or recurrent networks. In Ref. [42], they
present an attention-based spatiotemporal graph attention
network (ASTGAT) model for network degradation and
oversmoothing issues. In Ref. [43], the model relies on at-
tention to see connections between input and output. Re-
cently, attention mechanisms have also been used in graph
neural networks. In Ref. [44], they introduced gated at-
tention networks for graph learning. In Ref. [45], a brand-
new GCN dubbed TFM-GCAM incorporates attention
mechanisms to better capture nodes’ dynamic properties
and spatial–temporal attributes.
7. Conclusions and Future Work
In this paper, we proposed a new approach to trafc fow
prediction using a deep learning model called MASTGCNet.
To address the complexities of trafc, we introduced a dy-
namic graph generation component and a spatiotemporal
multiscale feature extraction component to the standard
GCNs. Tese components help the model learn specifc
patterns for each point and understand relationships at
diferent levels of detail in the data. We performed exper-
iments using baseline techniques on two extensive trafc
fow datasets to confrm the efciency of our MASTGCNet
model. Te experimental outcomes afrm the MASTGCNet
model’s performance and the proposed MUST module.
MASTGCNet implements a resource allocation strategy
within edge computing to minimize energy consumption
during prediction.
In the future, we aim to increase the model simplicity to
facilitate its seamless application to related tasks. Tis ap-
proach is intended to strengthen the model’s performance
and capacity for broader applicability. In addition, we plan
to improve our model by integrating external factors, such as
unexpected events and weather conditions, to increase its
predictive accuracy.
